label: input token r during the original phase
explanation: Single-token detector: fires whenever the input is the letter r during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at any position and sequence length. Dev precision 1.0, recall 0.995, mass recall 0.9996. Magnitude is highest (near max) for the first r of the sequence, especially at early positions. It is lower on a repeated r (about 0.6-0.9 of max) and in sampled examples it is weak (about 0.15-0.25 of max) when r is the last original token right before <DEL>. It never fires on the delimiter or on any other token. In the copy phase it is essentially silent: when r is fed back as an output-input it gives only tiny activations (about 0.05-0.1 of max, 0.04% of mass), seen mainly at recall_idx 1.

issues: Minor: the claim that r is weak (about 0.15-0.25 of max) when it is the last original token is only directional. Of the to_go==0 r steps, 39% fall in the lowest activation quartile, but 18% fall in Q2 and 4% in Q3. So these steps are often weak, not always 0.15-0.25.
Minor: the claim that a repeated r is lower checks out. in_first==0 r steps sit in Q1 (19%) and Q2 (14%) and never reach Q4.

Copy-phase claim checks out. r fed back in the copy phase activates only 0.6% of the time, and those activations hold 0.04% of the mass. Test misses (520 steps) are all copy-phase r at about 0.0-0.09 of max, mainly at recall_idx 1. There are 0 false positives.
Test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.995, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9996. No systematic gap by token, position, length or history was found.
